meta.dataset: Jülich pedestrian dynamics archive: Bottleneck, Caserne (Düsseldorf, 2006)

papers.label: Seyfried, Rupprecht, Passon, Steffen, Klingsch, Boltes: New insights into pedestrian flow through bottlenecks. Transportation Science 43 (2009) 395-406
Seyfried et al.: Enhanced empirical data for the fundamental diagram and the flow through bottlenecks. PED 2008 (Springer 2010)
Liddle et al.: An experimental study of pedestrian congestions: influence of bottleneck width and length (arXiv 2009)

meta.method: PedPy compute_n_t on a measurement line; flow = (k1 - k0) / (t_k1 - t_k0) over the crossings ranked k0..k1 (1 / mean time gap); specific flow = flow / b. Same code (sim/bottleneck_flow.py) for the experiment and the simulation.
meta.measurement_line: bottleneck entrance, y = 0, from x = -b/2 to x = b/2
meta.steady_window: crossings 10 to 150: skips the first 9 people (start-up) and ends at the 150th person like Liddle et al. (2009)
meta.engine: JuPedSim 1.4.2 via the Showtime sim image (Tier 3)
meta.model: collision-free speed model (app default), with the app's squeeze and unstick rules active
meta.walk_speed: normal(1.34, 0.26) m/s clipped to 0.6-2.0; 5% slow walkers at 0.7 m/s
assumptions: Geometry from the archive metadata (wkt_geometry and parameters): corridor 7 m wide in front of the bottleneck, bottleneck b x l, walls 5 cm thick; coordinates in the archive's frame (entrance on y = 0).

The holding area is not specified in the metadata or papers: it spans the corridor width and ends 4 m before the entrance ('bottleneck_distance'); its depth gives an initial density of 3.3 persons/m2 (the value of the group's 2005 series, Seyfried et al. 2009), e.g. 7.36 m for 170 people.
Behind the bottleneck: an open area 8 m wide and 1 m deep (the metadata's bounding box), whose far edge is the exit, so the exit never limits the flow.
Everyone starts walking at t = 0 (no reaction-time spread); the participants were soldiers told to walk normally, the simulation uses the app's adult walking speeds.
Real trajectories are head positions at 25 fps; simulated positions are body centres at 4 fps (app default output rate).
meta.experimental_repeat: Run l4 repeats the b120 setup (b = 1.2 m, l = 4 m, 178 people): 2.36 /s measured with the same method
